next_step: final perf POC + security questionnaire review
notes:
Prospect: low-latency trading decisioning platform. Evaluating Redwood for sub-50ms P95 inference on small-context decisions + high QPS (2k-6k rps depending on market peaks).

Key pain: currently running ensembles of smaller models on in-house servers; cost and ops overhead high. Need predictable latency during market open spikes.

From call 2024-10-22: 'If we can't get consistent P95 <50ms at 1k concurrency, it's a non-starter.' Emphasis on deterministic tail latency, replayable audit trails.

Optimization asks: batching vs micro-batching (prefers continuous batching with strict SLOs), prefix/KV caching for repeated context, 8-bit quantization tradeoffs for throughput. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations and quantization profiles.

Perf benchmark requests: reproduce 3 workload profiles — (1) short decision payloads (32 tokens, 1k-2k rps), (2) mid-context support queries (128 tokens, 500 rps), (3) bursty ensemble reranking (ensemble of 3 models, 64 tokens each, peak 6k rps). Ask for p50/p95/p99 for latency, token throughput, and cost per 1M tokens.

Security: strict VPC + KMS, retention controls, SSO w/ Okta. Need SOC2+ISO27100 mapping doc.

Quote request timeline: need final pricing + SLA by 2024-12-10 to hit procurement cycle.

Last demo (2024-11-05): ran synthetic benchmark via Redwood Dedicated; initial numbers promising: p95 ~42ms for 32-token decision path at 1k concurrency using continuous batching + LLM quantized to int8 (observed ~1.8x throughput improvement). Team wants repeat run on customer data and isolation test on Private deployment.
